items.title: Anthropic migrated its Messages API from Python to Rust
items.summary: Anthropic describes migrating its Messages API from Python to Rust, using the production API as a verifier to find and fix differences on production traffic. The Rust API uses about 70% less CPU per request and cuts median time to first token by about 20% without taking the service offline or freezing feature development.

evidence.quote: We ran into this problem when we migrated our Messages API from Python to Rust.
From early 2024 to fall 2026, API traffic grew roughly 1,800 times.
Claude wrote a first version of the API’s core request path in about a week.
But building trust in the migration required us to find a way to verify that our Rust API was at parity with our production API.

In this post, we share how we turned the production Messages API itself into a verifier—and how that helped us test the new Rust version on production traffic, find where it differed, and automatically dispatch agents to fix those differences.

This allowed us to ship an API on Rust that uses about 70% less CPU per request and cuts median time to first token by about 20% without ever taking the service offline or freezing feature development.
The effort required to undertake the project was dropping fast: by May 2026, Claude was writing more than 80% of the code Anthropic merged .
Verification, not generation, had become the bottleneck.

items.title: Antom 3-in-1 Transformer is a payment foundation model
items.summary: Antom 3-in-1 Transformer integrates sequence, tabular, and graph representations for payment risk detection, with approximately 7B parameters and approximately 1.7B activated per task route. In a four-month online experiment on Ant International's billion-scale payment platform, it reduced the overall loss rate by 37.88% relative to XGB-Online, and no model weights are released.

items.title: LlamaIndex released OCRia-nano-1 for CPU document parsing
items.summary: OCRia-nano-1 is an 8.1M-parameter model pipeline for document parsing on CPU from LlamaIndex, pairing a detector-recognizer OCR stack with LayoutNet inside the open-source local parser LiteParse. Its models are distilled from OCRia-1, the 4B document VLM, and it scores 59.2 on ParseBench-2 while running at 27.8 pages per second on 16 vCPUs.

evidence.quote: OCRia-nano-1 is an 8.1M-parameter model pipeline for document parsing on CPU from LlamaIndex .
It pairs a detector–recognizer OCR stack with LayoutNet, a joint table and layout model, and it runs inside
LiteParse , the open-source local document parser.
Its models are distilled
from OCRia-1 , our 4B document VLM, with 1/500th of its parameters.
Accuracy: 59.2 on ParseBench-2 , ahead of the CPU parsers Indra (55.1) and
It lifts LiteParse from 48.7 with Tesseract.
Speed: 27.8 pages per second on 16 vCPUs, 426 ms per page on one core, twice as fast as LiteParse with Tesseract.
Tables and layout: LayoutNet finds tables (rows, columns, spanning header cells) and classifies layout blocks
(headings, lists, captions, page headers and footers) on scanned and born-digital pages.
Scripts: a router sends each text line to one of four recognizers: Latin, CJK, right-to-left (Arabic, Hebrew),
and a world-script model for about 17 more scripts.
CPU runtime, everywhere LiteParse runs: the CLI, Python and Node.js on Linux, macOS and Windows, and the browser and
edge runtimes through WebAssembly.
These are the model files LiteParse runs; they are not a standalone model with its own inference script.

items.title: LlamaIndex released OCRia-1, a 4B document parsing model
items.summary: OCRia-1 is a 4B vision-language model from LlamaIndex that reads a page image and writes the page as Markdown with tables in HTML, in one call per page and without a layout detector, OCR engine, or text layer. It scores 85.2 on ParseBench 2 and 84.7 on ParseBench 1, and this repository holds the unoptimized BF16 weights.

evidence.quote: OCRia-1 is a 4B vision-language model for document parsing from LlamaIndex .
It reads a page
image and writes the page as Markdown, with tables in HTML, and it is built for the content that document parsers get
wrong most often: merged cells and spanning headers, tables with thousands of cells, charts whose data has to be read
off the plot, and formatting that carries meaning, such as strikethrough, underline, sub- and superscripts and
Accuracy: the highest-scoring open-weight model on both ParseBench leaderboards, with
visual grounding included: 85.2 on ParseBench 2 (six dimensions, seventh of 61 systems) and 84.7 on ParseBench 1
(five dimensions, second of 158).
One call per page: the text comes from the page image alone, with no layout detector, OCR engine or text layer.
This repository holds the unoptimized BF16 weights .
To run OCRia-1 on your own machine with llama.cpp or Ollama (Linux, Windows, macOS), use the GGUF builds in
llamaindex/OCRia-1-GGUF ; the Q8_0 build scores the same as these
weights on a ParseBench 2 sample.

items.title: MemTensor released MemT-1.0-Pro memory foundation models
items.summary: MemT-1.0 integrates dynamic local memory and trainable hyper memory to retain historical information without accessing original context at inference, keeping persistent state constant in size. Its storage use drops by approximately 66× versus a full-context KV cache at 128K history length, and it introduces an agentic framework for experience-guided agentic coding.

evidence.quote: 🚀🚀 We are happy to announce the release of MemT-1.0-Pro [MemT × NVIDIA]!
MemT-1.0 is a new generation of memory foundation models that makes persistent, dynamically evolving memory an intrinsic part of model computation.
MemT-1.0 integrates dynamic local memory and trainable hyper memory to retain and leverage historical information without accessing original context at inference.
Its persistent state remains constant in size, reducing storage by approximately 66× versus full-context KV cache at 128K history length.
The project makes three main contributions:
Introduce MemT-1.0 with improved memory storage and utilization, and Mixture-of-Storage (MoS) for scalable memory capacity.
Develop backbone preparation and a two-stage training pipeline, supported by 34B tokens of data and dedicated infrastructure.
Study memory scaling and demonstrate native memory for experience-guided agentic coding.
Qwen3.6-35B-A3B
NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B
Experience-Guided Agentic Coding
MemT-1.0 introduces an agentic framework for reusing procedural experience in long-horizon coding tasks.
Retrieved experience is stored in native memory and accessed through memory attention during execution, improving task performance without adding experience text to the task context.

items.title: NightWatch gives computer-use agents continuous perception
items.summary: NightWatch is a plug-and-play framework that pairs a vision-language agent with NightWatch-0.8B, a lightweight System-1 model performing streaming monitoring of the interface state, without changing the agent's model, prompt, or action space. On OSWorld it reduces non-reasoning wall-clock time by 33% and wasted time by 53% while keeping task success on par, and raises success on DynaCU-Bench from 39.5% to 44.2% with the large VLM agent.

evidence.quote: To bridge this gap, we present NightWatch, a plug-and-play framework that endows any CUA with continuous, temporally grounded perception without changing the agent's model, prompt, or action space.

NightWatch couples the VLM agent with NightWatch-0.8B , a lightweight System-1 model that performs streaming monitoring of the interface state and keeps the agent synchronized with the evolving environment at low computational cost and latency, thereby grounding each decision in the current state ra
ther than an outdated snapshot and reducing both stale actions and idle waiting while preserving task success.

Experiments on desktop and dynamic web environments (OSWorld-Verified and DynaCU-Bench) show that NightWatch, driven by a watcher of only 0.8B parameters, reduces non-reasoning wall-clock time by 33% and wasted time by 53% on OSWorld while keeping task success on par, raises success on DynaCU-Bench

from 39.5% to 44.2% with the large VLM agent , and is more efficient than passive-watching baselines such as AOI and PUSV under the same screenshot-only input , as well as a System-1 decision model more than 30times its size.

items.title: RLVB teaches agents to commit only when evidence is sufficient
items.summary: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Beliefs (RLVB) rewards an agent for taking further steps while the exact posterior over the answer still allows several answers and for committing once the evidence is sufficient, without a judge, critic, or reward model. It improves the base model in all nine settings by 17.1% on average and outperforms PPO with a process reward from an LLM judge by 9.3% on average while using 1.6 times fewer GPU-hours.

evidence.quote: During training, however, the simulator can compute the exact posterior over the answer at every step and tell whether the evidence is already enough.

We propose Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Beliefs (RLVB) , which rewards the agent for taking further steps while this posterior still allows several answers and for committing once the evidence is sufficient.
The reward needs no judge, critic or reward model , and it never reads the belief line the agent writes before each action.
We also introduce Pro Worlds , a benchmark of visual puzzles where the agent views a large world through a small window.
We evaluate three vision-language models on three benchmarks, two of which are never seen in training.
RLVB improves the base model in all nine settings, by 17.1% on average.
RLVB also outperforms PPO with a process reward from an LLM judge by 9.3% on average while using 1.6 times fewer GPU-hours .

items.title: S-Mind internalizes multi-view geometry for spatial intelligence
items.summary: S-Mind internalizes multi-view geometry inside a multimodal large language model through a compact set of spatial tokens that hold a fused 3D scene and re-emit it from each reasoning viewpoint. Across four spatial benchmarks it improves its Qwen3.5 backbones by up to 22.26 points and runs about 100x faster than a tool-based agent on the same backbone.

items.title: Loom attention lets Transformers rewire circuits per token
items.summary: Loom attention lets a Transformer dynamically rewire its circuits at every token by combining a head's vertical attention over earlier head outputs with its horizontal attention over tokens, yielding the dual-stream LoomFormer architecture. Trained on the same 300B tokens with only 2% extra FLOPs, LoomPythia-2.8B achieves ~1.6x the average downstream gain of mHC-Pythia-2.8B over Pythia-2.8B.

items.title: ICLWorld benchmarks in-context learning from digital to physical worlds
items.summary: ICLWorld is an online benchmark with UIverse, a unified harness that turns every environment into a user interface, covering computer use and robot use with 30 environments, 630 demonstration videos, and 160 tasks with customized rules. The strongest agents, Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, succeed on 82% and 76% of computer-use runs but only 27% and 26% of robot-use runs.

evidence.quote: Generated by deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash In-context learning (ICL) lets agents acquire new rules from context and adapt to user-specific requirements at inference time .

We present ICLWorld, an online benchmark that evaluates the ICL of agents from digital to physical worlds, covering computer use and robot use, together with UIverse, a unified harness that turns every environment into a user interface.
We build 30 environments, record 630 demonstration videos (10+ hours), and design 160 tasks with customized, often counter-intuitive rules that cannot be satisfied without learning from the context.
Each task comes with three rule versions, given as text or video, and we test generalization at three levels, from replaying the demonstration to new instances and unseen environments.

Across six frontier models , the strongest agents , Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, succeed on 82% and 76% of computer-use runs but only 27% and 26% of robot-use runs, and a no-rule control reduces success to at most 8%.
These findings reveal substantial gaps between the digital and the physical world and between identifying a rule and acting on it.

items.title: CoT-Proxy distills long-horizon policies without hidden reasoning
items.summary: CoT-Proxy shows that a long-horizon policy can be distilled from a teacher's actions alone, with the student trained on trajectories whose reasoning block is left empty, an effect the authors call cross-format transfer. Distilling the actions of Qwen3.6-27B raises Qwen3-4B on AppWorld from 7% to 18%, CoT-proxies raise it further to 35%, and distilling GPT-5.6 Luna raises it to 48%.

items.title: ACAP organizes a robot as a team of persistent coding agents
items.summary: Asynchronous Coding Agents as Policy (ACAP) organizes one robot as a team of persistent agents, each handling a configurable control group, with a hyper-agent assigning tasks, coordinating dependencies, and allocating control. Across 72 real-world rollouts covering 25 task/platform settings, ACAP reduces task-balanced time cost by 28.2% compared with a single-agent Direct Policy.

items.title: PartAgent segments 3D parts with experts and closed-loop refinement
items.summary: PartAgent is a training-free agentic framework for 3D part segmentation that combines regions from a 3D expert with multiview semantic evidence from a 2D expert and refines partitions through observation-driven closed-loop actions. On PartObjaverse-Tiny-WT it achieves 68.41 mIoU, and across 3DCoMPaT200, PartNeXt, PartNetE, and PartObjaverse-Tiny it averages 69.36 mIoU.

evidence.quote: We present PartAgent, a training-free agentic framework for 3D part segmentation built upon two complementary modules: (i) Structural-Semantic Expert Integration combines regions predicted by the 3D expert with multiview semantic evidence from the 2D expert through image-to-surface correspondences ,
constructing compositional part partitions at multiple granularities.

(ii) Observation-Driven Closed-Loop Partition Refinement observes the current partition and its supporting evidence to select targeted inspection, evidence repair, composition, or reselection actions.
It verifies proposed changes and uses the updated state and action outcomes to guide subsequent decisions.
On PartObjaverse-Tiny-WT, PartAgent achieves 68.41 mIoU , outperforming the strongest competing method by 8.53 points.

Across 3DCoMPaT200, PartNeXt, PartNetE, and PartObjaverse-Tiny, PartAgent achieves the highest mIoU on each dataset, averaging 69.36 across the four datasets, 7.28 points above the highest mean among competing methods.

items.title: SpecEngineeringBench evaluates coding agents as specification engineers
items.summary: SpecEngineeringBench comprises 100 instances from 78 open-source Python repositories across 16 application categories, with independent tasks for generating test suites and discovering defects through execution analysis. Across seven frontier coding agents, test validity and coverage decouple from defect exposure: agents reach a 91.47% Head Pass Rate and 80.48% Change-focused Coverage alongside a 26.36% Fail-to-Pass Rate.

items.title: Qwen-Image-HD generates high-resolution images blockwise
items.summary: Qwen-Image-HD adapts Qwen-Image 2.0 to high-resolution synthesis through local training and blockwise autoregressive generation, with each prediction covering a target tile at 1K scale conditioned on upper and left neighbors and a compressed thumbnail. On Qwen-Image-Bench at 4K it achieves stronger overall evaluation performance than direct 4K generation with FLUX-3-Image-Klein.

items.title: Google Research open-sourced a verifiable social reasoning benchmark
items.summary: Google Research introduces an evaluation framework based on multi-agent social simulations, where a target agent with a hidden motive interacts with other agents including one representing the user, who then asks the evaluated assistant to infer the motive, providing verifiable ground truth by construction. The framework and a dataset with over 20K generated examples are open-sourced.

evidence.quote: We introduce an evaluation framework based on multi-agent social simulations that quantifies how well AI assistants understand social situations from users' subjective narratives.

In our framework, a target agent with a hidden motive interacts with other agents including one representing the user, who then consults the evaluated assistant to infer the target’s motive, providing verifiable ground truth by construction.
Designed to address both of these challenges, we introduce an evaluation framework for social reasoning based on multi-agent simulations.
In our framework, a target agent is assigned a hidden motive and interacts with other agents, including one representing the user.
The user then consults with the evaluated assistant, which must infer the target's hidden motive.
Evaluating a diverse range of LLMs through our framework reveals that relying on subjective user mediation substantially complicates social reasoning.
Furthermore, models are sensitive to user framing, require more detail than humans need to reach correct predictions, and fail to fully leverage clarification questions.
We open-source the framework and dataset to encourage future research on user-mediated social reasoning.

items.title: CodecOPSD prunes redundant condition tokens for video generation
items.summary: On-Policy Codec Distillation (CodecOPSD) combines a codec-based token pruning method with an on-policy self-distillation strategy that trains a DiT adapter to learn the pruning pattern without quality degradation. Scaled to 16 condition modalities, it prunes 66% of condition tokens on average, making denoising 2x faster and shrinking cache memory by up to 73% in KV cache mode.
